Article Title: West Bengal to be renamed 'Paschim Banga'? Proposal to be tabled in Assembly on Dec 9: CM Suvendu
Article Text:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari

West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday announced that a resolution to rename the state as ‘Paschim Banga’ will be moved in the Assembly on December 9. The state Cabinet approved the proposal at a meeting earlier in the day.Speaking to ANI reporters in Kolkata, Adhikari said the resolution would be introduced during the Assembly’s winter session, scheduled from December 4 to 14. He also clarified that ‘Paschim Banga’ would be the state's name in English.“In English, too, West Bengal will be ‘Paschim Banga’. ‘Paschim Banga’—it must be written exactly as is. We are bringing a resolution to the Legislative Assembly on the 9th; following that, it will go to the Government of India and then to Parliament,” he told the news agency.The chief minister said the proposed change was linked to the state's history and its formation in 1947.“This is a matter of history—the history surrounding the formation of West Bengal, which took place in 1947. This change is something that ought to happen. Instead of ‘West Bengal’, it will be ‘Paschim Banga’,” he added.If passed by the state Assembly, the resolution will be sent to the Centre for approval. The renaming will require clearance from the central government and Parliament before it can formally take effect.The announcement follows remarks by West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya in October, when he indicated that the state would be renamed.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that a resolution to rename the state as ‘Paschim Banga’ will be moved in the Assembly on December 9. The state Cabinet approved the proposal at a meeting earlier in the day. If passed by the state Assembly, the resolution will be sent to the Centre for approval.

Article Title: 'Stop acting like Baahubali': SC raps Bihar judicial officer for FIR against SP for disobeying directions
Article Text:
SC pulled up a Bihar judge for convicting an SP over non-compliance with directions to register an FIR

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday pulled up a Bihar judicial officer for convicting a police officer over non-compliance with directions to register an FIR. The top court questioned his understanding of contempt law and telling him not to "act like a Baahubali" while exercising judicial powers. The bench also suggested that the judicial officer be sent for training to the National Judicial Academy."Ask your client to stop acting like a 'Bahubali' while exercising judicial powers," Chief Justice Surya Kant said while hearing the judicial officer's plea against a Patna high court order staying his decision.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana criticised district and additional sessions judge-IV, Rohtas at Sasaram, Anil Kumar for convicting the police officer on the same day and treating the non-compliance as an offence committed in the face of the court."We are really surprised at your understanding of law. You must first understand the scope and ambit of Section 384 BNSS and Section 345 CrPC. If someone slaps someone or abuses the court, or refuses to leave the courtroom when directed, that is an offence committed in the face of the court. But if we direct someone to register an FIR and they do not, it does not amount to a crime committed in the face of the court," news agency PTI quoted the bench as saying."Your understanding of law is appalling. You also took such an aggressive stance, called the superintendent and convicted him on the same day," Justice Bagchi said.Questioning the judge's objection to an inspecting judge's intervention, Justice Bagchi said, "Were you within your domain and jurisdiction when you called the district magistrate and superintendent of police, treated their non-appearance as an offence committed in the face of the court and convicted and sentenced him? You also stay your hands.Enough of adventure."On September 29, 2026, Anil Kumar convicted IPS officer Raushan Kumar, then superintendent of police (SP) of Rohtas, for wilfully disobeying court directions to register an FIR against a person who had allegedly given false evidence in a criminal case decided in 2023.The judicial officer imposed a symbolic fine of Rs 1 on the SP and directed Bihar's director general of police (DGP) to enter the court's observations into the officer's service records. He also called on the Union ministry of personnel and training to overhaul the training of IAS and IPS officers to better align them with a democratic setup.The Patna high court had subsequently stayed the order imposing the fine on the SP for contempt of court.
Article Summary: The top court questioned his understanding of contempt law and told him not to "act like a Baahubali" while exercising judicial powers. The bench suggested that the judicial officer be sent for training to the National Judicial Academy. On September 29, 2026, Anil Kumar convicted IPS officer Raushan Kumar, then superintendent of police (SP) of Rohtas.

NEW DELHI: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday expressed confidence that the Congress would return to power in the state by winning 90 of the 119 Assembly seats in the 2028 elections. Addressing the party's Political Affairs Committee (PAC) meeting in Hyderabad, he said the Congress leadership was preparing a strategy to strengthen the organisation and secure another term in office."Congress will secure 90 seats with one crore votes in the next assembly elections", the CM asserted.Reddy also told the newly-appointed AICC in-charge of party affairs in Telangana, BM Sandeep, that the state Congress should work towards making Rahul Gandhi the prime minister.He said Telangana would contribute 15 Lok Sabha seats to the Congress in the 2029 general elections, provided the total number of constituencies in the state remained at 17."You have to convey our consensus to Kharge ji, Rahul ji and Sonia ji," he told Sandeep.Revanth Reddy targets BRS over 'false propaganda'The chief minister also criticised the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), accusing its leadership of spreading false narratives against the Congress government in an attempt to return to power.Taking a dig at BRS leaders over their recent protest outside the Assembly, where they took off their shirts after being stopped by the police, Reddy said, "BRS leaders took off their shirts outside the Assembly building recently (when they were stopped by police), and now their trousers will be removed.Warns Congress leaders against public criticismAgainst the backdrop of criticism from some ruling party leaders over his government, Reddy warned Congress members against making negative remarks about the government in public."We are closely observing everyone’s behaviour and the way they speak. The party has complete information on what each leader says in public and in private," he said.He added that leaders who remained aligned with the party's position would receive organisational and other posts in due course.Says Congress could have formed government at Centre in 2024Recalling the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Reddy said he had correctly predicted that the BJP would not cross 240 seats.He argued that had the BJP won 25 fewer seats, and the Congress secured 25 more, the Congress would have formed the government at the Centre.Reddy also recalled that former prime minister Indira Gandhi represented Medak in Telangana as a Lok Sabha member when she was assassinated in 1984. He said the state Congress should now resolve to make Rahul Gandhi the prime minister.Government preparing drought action planThe chief minister said the state government would reach out to people directly after the Sankranti festival in January 2027.He also said the government was preparing an action plan to address possible drought conditions caused by the adverse impact of the El Niño phenomenon.Reddy highlighted the welfare schemes being implemented by his government and recalled the challenges faced by Congress workers during the previous BRS regime.

NEW DELHI: Congress and Samajwadi Party (SP) concluded the first round of seat-sharing talks for 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections on Monday, with the top leaders describing it as "positive". The two parties are likely to finalise their agreement within the next two to four days, leaders of the two parties said, news agency PTI reported.SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, who is heading the party's talks panel, said both sides had exchanged views and were optimistic about reaching an agreement soon."We expect to complete the alliance within the next two to three days. The second round of talks will be held tomorrow," PTI quoted Yadav as saying.The meeting was held at the residence of Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari in the national capital. Leaders said the talks were progressing in a cordial atmosphere, but did not disclose the number of seats either party is seeking.Congress' Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam also described the meeting as positive and said an agreement was close."The meeting went very well and was positive. We will reach an agreement very soon... it is almost finalised," he said."Since the talks are progressing positively, we will not comment on other details, and we will not disclose the seat-sharing details at this stage," he added.Gautam said the two parties would hold another meeting on Tuesday.Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Misra-Mona also expressed confidence that the arrangement would be finalised soon."I am not talking about numbers. Numbers are not important. ... we will meet again tomorrow, and everything will be finalised," she said, adding that the parties were likely to conclude the process within two to four days.Elections to the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly are due early next year. Chief minister Yogi Adityanath is seeking a third consecutive term, while the SP and Congress are looking to challenge the BJP's dominance in the state.The Congress and SP are working towards a joint contest in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The Congress is seeking a larger share of seats, citing the outcome of the last Lok Sabha elections and Rahul Gandhi's position as a prominent opposition leader nationally.The SP's negotiation panel is headed by Ram Gopal Yadav and includes party state president Shyam Lal Pal and Lok Sabha MPs Rajiv Rai and Iqra Choudhary. Neither party has disclosed the number of seats being discussed.The two parties contested the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections independently.
Article Summary: Congress and Samajwadi Party hold first round of seat-sharing talks for 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Leaders of the two parties describe talks as "positive" and expect agreement in next few days. Neither party has disclosed the number of seats being discussed. Congress seeking larger share of seats, citing outcome of last Lok Sabha elections and Rahul Gandhi's position as prominent opposition leader nationally.

NEW DELHI: Congress general secretary and Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot on Monday termed the reported possibility of a renewed alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in Punjab as “pure opportunism”, questioning what had changed since the two parties parted ways.He also criticised the Bhagwant Mann-led Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government and said Congress could provide an alternative ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Addressing the media in Amritsar, Pilot questioned whether the issues that led to the BJP and Akali Dal ending their alliance had been resolved.“Look, the Bharatiya Janata Party has said all those things against the Akali Dal when their mutual agreement ended and for what reasons the alliance between the Akali Dal and BJP had broken. Have all those reasons disappeared?” he asked.Referring to reports of a possible reunion, he said, “The question that arises is: what caused the alliance to break, and what has changed today that you are going to form an alliance again?”Pilot alleged that both parties were struggling to regain their political footing in Punjab after facing rejection in Assembly and Lok Sabha elections.“Now, out of compulsion, they are holding each other's hands right before the elections,” he said.He also referred to the controversy over the three farm laws and allegations concerning drugs, asking the two parties to explain their political differences to voters.“I understand that you were separate for all five years, but what were all the things said regarding the three black laws on drugs? So many people lost their lives in the protest. The Akali Dal and the BJP should answer why they are together today. But I believe this is pure opportunism,” Pilot said.Turning his criticism towards the AAP government, Pilot said its tenure had run its course and claimed voters were looking for a change in Punjab. He also questioned Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's handling of issues in the state.“The Chief Minister has only told jokes and made lighthearted comments over the last five years. Action should be taken seriously on all issues. They haven't done that,” he said.Describing Punjab as “a border state, a very sensitive state”, Pilot said it needed a responsible government. He added that Congress could offer voters an alternative.“The people of Punjab want change, and the Aam Aadmi Party government's term is completely over. The public wants change, and change will happen, along with a better alternative system. If anyone can do it, the Congress party can,” he said.On Congress's preparations for the 2027 polls, Pilot said the State Election Committee would meet on Tuesday and that a screening committee had been formed. Candidates, he said, would be selected on merit, feedback and their prospects of winning.He also expressed confidence that the Congress-Samajwadi Party alliance would continue in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, with seat-sharing talks expected to be finalised soon.
Article Summary: Congress general secretary and Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot calls reported possibility of a renewed alliance between BJP and Akali Dal 'pure opportunism' Pilot also criticised the Bhagwant Mann-led Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government and said Congress could provide an alternative ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

NEW DELHI: Independent MP Pappu Yadav on Sunday criticised the BJP and Bihar government for naming a newly built bridge after former chief minister Nitish Kumar . He said that if the government genuinely respected the veteran JD(U) leader, it should make his son, Nishant Kumar, the chief minister."If you have so much respect for Nitish Kumar, then I urge you to make Nishant Kumar the chief minister. They came to power in Nitish Kumar's name. Why did you stab him in the back? Article Title: 'Destroyed credibility of polls': Congress alleges gaps in voting data across 200 seats in Lok Sabha polls
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday stepped up its attack on the Centre, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah, through Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, had "destroyed" the credibility of Indian elections.In a post on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh reiterated the party's demand for Kumar's resignation, saying PM Modi and Shah must be held accountable for "vote chori"."An investigation has revealed that ECI's internal records are missing for voters who voted after 5 pm in 200 seats in Maharashtra, Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir in 2024. The returning officer's reports contain no figures for the final hour of polling," he wrote.Ramesh claimed that the number of votes polled was supposed to be tallied every two hours to prevent manipulation, but alleged that this procedure was not followed.He also questioned the increase in voter turnout recorded after 5 pm, citing Maharashtra, where the final turnout was 76 lakh votes higher than the figures reported at 5 pm."These late evening votes have already been suspect for bogus voting: in Maharashtra, the final turnout was 76 lakh votes higher than (the figures) reported at 5 pm.How is this possible? For one assembly, Kopri-Pachpakhadi, it means one vote was cast every 15 seconds at each booth for a full hour," Ramesh said."The Modi-Shah duo, through CEC Gyanesh Kumar, have destroyed the credibility of India's elections. They must be held accountable for this grave crime against our democracy. The CEC must resign, and the duo must answer for vote chori," he added.Meanwhile, Congress has announced a series of programmes to step up its campaign against alleged electoral irregularities.The party will organise 'Samvidhan Raksha (Save Constitution)' marches across states on November 26, observed as Constitution Day. It will also launch a booth-level verification drive to check deleted voter names and hold village-level 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao (Save Elections, Save India)' chaupals.In a circular issued to Pradesh Congress Committee presidents, general secretaries, in-charges and other key office bearers, Congress general secretary (organisation) K C Venugopal said state committees would organise 'Samvidhan Raksha' marches on November 26.Ahead of the marches, Congress workers will undertake a 'Vote Rakshak' campaign, visiting every polling booth to verify the names of voters whose names have been deleted from electoral rolls.From November 29 to December 15, the party will organise village-level 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' chaupals based on the findings of the verification campaign.
Article Summary: PM Modi and home minister Amit Shah must be held accountable for "vote chori," says Congress general secretary. Congress has announced a series of programmes to step up its campaign against alleged electoral irregularities. The party will organise 'Samvidhan Raksha (Save Constitution)' marches across states on November 26, observed as Constitution Day.

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned seven serving and retired Punjab government officials, including IAS and IPS officers, for questioning in a money-laundering case against suspended state DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar, officials said on Sunday.Of the seven officials summoned, five are currently serving in the government, while the others have retired.The ED is also investigating their alleged links with Bhullar's aide, Krishanu Sharda, who has been arrested in the case.Kumar Rahul, secretary in Punjab's health and family welfare department, has been asked to appear before the ED on Monday, while Anand Sagar, staff officer to the commissioner of Faridkot division, has been summoned on November 25. Neeru Katyal Gupta, special secretary in the General Administration and Coordination Department, is scheduled to appear on November 26.The agency has also summoned two police officers. Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh has been called for questioning on November 26, while Ludhiana Police Commissioner Swapan Sharma has been asked to appear the following day.The two retired officials summoned are former bureaucrats.Gurpreet Sapra, who previously served as the Jalandhar Commissioner, has been asked to appear on November 26. Arun Sekhri, who served as divisional commissioner for Faridkot, Ferozepur and Jalandhar, has been summoned for questioning on November 25.The money-laundering case against Bhullar under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) stems from two FIRs registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) against him and his associates over alleged bribery and possession of assets disproportionate to their known sources of income.Bhullar, who was serving as Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police, Ropar Range, was arrested by the CBI in October 2025. The arrest followed a complaint by a scrap dealer who alleged that a bribe had been demanded from him through an intermediary to settle a case.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned seven serving and retired Punjab government officials, including IAS and IPS officers. The officials are being questioned in a money-laundering case against suspended state DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar. Article Title: Son of Delhi doctor accused of killing domestic help dies; father moves court for interim bail
Article Text:
In photos: The accused Dr Manish Gupta; the victim domestic help





NEW DELHI: Dr Manish Gupta, an accused in the domestic help murder case, has approached a Delhi court seeking three weeks' interim bail following the death of his 19-year-old son, Parth Gupta, on November 19.Gupta has sought temporary release to attend his son's last rites and be with his family during the bereavement. He is currently in judicial custody after being arrested by Delhi Police on June 18, 2026, and is facing trial in the murder case before Saket District Court.Additional Sessions Judge Anuj Aggarwal took note of the application and directed Delhi Police to submit a verification report. The court has listed the matter for hearing on Saturday.Moving the application on Gupta's behalf, advocate Kamal Nayan Tiwari submitted that the accused was facing an extremely difficult situation following the sudden death of his only child. He argued that Gupta, as the deceased's father, had an emotional and moral responsibility to attend the last rites, but his continued custody had prevented him from doing so.The counsel told the court that he received a call from Gupta's wife on November 20, informing him that their 19-year-old son had died a day earlier. The application stated that the death had come as a devastating shock to the family and that Gupta was unable to be present with them because he was in custody.Parth was also named as a suspect in the charge sheet filed by Delhi Police in the domestic help murder case and had been questioned during the investigation.
Article Summary: Dr Manish Gupta, an accused in the domestic help murder case, has approached a Delhi court seeking three weeks' interim bail. His 19-year-old son, Parth Gupta, died on November 19. Gupta is currently in judicial custody after being arrested by Delhi Police on June 18, 2026.

Article Title: Rajasthan Congress chief demands CM Sharma resign over panchayat poll setback
Article Text:

JAIPUR: Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) president Govind Singh Dotasra Friday demanded the resignation of chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma and his cabinet, terming BJP’s setback in panchayat elections as “public anger” over alleged corruption, administrative lapses and unfulfilled promises.Addressing a news conference at the Congress office in Jaipur, Dotasra said the state govt was focused on optics rather than governance. “The state govt appears more interested in publicity and ceremonial events than addressing people’s problems,” he said.Taking aim at Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s earlier description of BJP’s urban local body performance as a “landslide victory,” Dotasra argued the results did not support the claim. He said BJP’s lead over Congress was marginal and claimed that “nearly 64% of voters voted against it” in the urban polls.“People have exposed the PM’s claim (in rural polls). Modi should be wary of the ‘facts’ fed to him by Rajasthan BJP, which only ends up embarrassing him,” Dotasra said.He reiterated his demand for resignations, saying, “If the CM and his ministers have even a little moral responsibility left, they should resign and tell the PM and the Union home minister that they have failed to meet the expectations of Rajasthan’s people.”Dotasra alleged the Sharma govt failed to address inflation, healthcare, fertiliser and seed availability for farmers, employment and women’s safety. Referring to alleged irregularities in medicines and medical equipment supplied to pregnant women, he accused the govt of evading accountability for maternal deaths. He also alleged that job seekers were facing police action. The language he used against a former CM was unacceptable. Even a street drunkard would not use such language,” Dotasra said.Questioning Sharma’s emphasis on high-profile visits and public events, Dotasra took a swipe at the ceremonial aspects of VIP tours. “A ‘Radhe Radhe’ stole, a memento, a helicopter ride and visits by the PM and the Union HM—but what did Rajasthan’s people get? You are not running an event management company; you are running a govt,” he said.
Article Summary: Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) president Govind Singh Dotasra Friday demanded the resignation of chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma and his cabinet. He terming BJP’s setback in panchayat elections as “public anger” over alleged corruption, administrative lapses and unfulfilled promises.

Article Title: Receipt of complaint by magistrate cannot be treated as order for investigation: HC
Article Text:
Bengaluru





: The receipt of the complaint by the magistrate cannot be treated as an order authorising investigation, Karnataka high court has observed in a recent judgment while granting relief to three accused persons.The petitioners, two of them from Goa and one from Telangana, contended that after the registration of the complaint at 7.30pm on Dec 9, 2024, the same was forwarded to the magistrate at 8.05pm. No written permission for prosecution was granted by the magistrate, they added.After perusing the materials on record, Justice Govindaraj noted that the First Schedule to the BNSS classifies the offence under BNS Section 318(3) as non-cognisable and bailable.Section 174(1) of the BNSS requires the officer in charge of a police station, upon receiving information concerning a non-cognisable offence, to enter the substance of such information in the prescribed book, refer the informant to the magistrate and forward the daily diary report of such cases to the magistrate fortnightly. More importantly, Section 174(2) of the BNSS expressly provides that no police officer shall investigate a non-cognisable case without an order of the magistrate having the power to try such case or commit the case for trial.The requirement of obtaining an order from the jurisdictional magistrate is, therefore, mandatory, the judge further pointed out.In the present case, the magistrate had not passed any order. Merely forwarding the complaint to the magistrate and obtaining an acknowledgement of its receipt does not amount to compliance with Section 174(2) of the BNSS. The statutory requirement is not one of mere intimation to the magistrate, but of obtaining an order authorising investigation. In the absence of such an order, police could not have proceeded in the manner adopted in the present case, the judge further observed while quashing the proceedings against the petitioners.
Article Summary: The petitioners, two of them from Goa and one from Telangana, contended that after the registration of the complaint at 7.30pm on Dec 9, 2024, the same was forwarded to the magistrate at 8.05pm. No written permission for prosecution was granted by the magistrate, they added.

Article Title: ED summons 2 AAP MLAs in probe into NH-754A land acquisition fraud
Article Text:
Enforcement Directorate has summoned Aam Aadmi Party's Amandeep Kaur Arora and Devinderjit Singh Ladi Dhos





BATHINDA: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned Aam Aadmi Party MLAs Amandeep Kaur Arora and Devinderjit Singh Ladi Dhos, apart from family members of MLA Amandeep Kaur Arora and some serving and retired government officials, in a matter pertaining to land acquisition for a portion of National Highway 754A.Arora and her family members have also been summoned in a probe pertaining to money laundering.The ED has asked Devinderjit Singh Dhos, MLA from the Dharamkot assembly constituency, to appear at its Chandigarh zonal office on November 27 over his alleged beneficial interest in land dealings and irregularities concerning compensation for crematorium land in Dharamkot.Amandeep Kaur Arora has been summoned to depose on November 26 on allegations that she is the main beneficiary of fraudulent land transfers and the diversion of land compensation money. Arora's husband, Rakesh Arora, has been summoned for November 25 over his alleged involvement in fraudulent property deals.Her father, Jaspal Singh, brother, Valjinder Singh, and maternal uncle, Harminder Singh, have been asked to appear before the agency on November 27, November 30 and December 2, respectively, for allegedly being beneficiaries of dubious property transactions.Earlier, an ED team had conducted searches for 36 hours at seven locations linked to Amandeep Kaur Arora on November 4-5.After the searches, the MLA had accused the BJP of being behind the ED action to scare and lure her.Among the government officials called for questioning are Moga District Revenue Officer Gurdev Singh Dham, Patwari Nirvair Singh and former Tehsildar Lakhwinder Singh.They have been summoned over alleged irregularities in assessing and disbursing compensation for land acquisition, fraudulent mutations, and the registration of sale deeds for government, municipal corporation and church trust lands despite objections.One Lakhwinder, a partner and director of a hospital-cum-de-addiction centre linked to the MLA, has also been asked to appear on November 30 over unaccounted cash collections, financial transactions, and the procurement and dispensing of psychotropic medicines.According to sources, the probe pertains to the alleged siphoning of compensation funds for land acquired to construct a section of National Highway 754A.The ED case originates from an FIR registered at Dharamkot police station on June 16, 2024, over the alleged manipulation of revenue records relating to government land and the wrongful disbursement of more than Rs 1 crore in compensation by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).Amandeep Kaur Arora, refuting the allegations, said the action was due to vendetta by the BJP, claiming that during the searches, ED officials repeatedly pressured her to join the BJP and promised her a ministerial position in return.Both Dhos and Arora have been re-nominated by the AAP from their respective assembly constituencies to contest the upcoming assembly elections.
Article Summary: Arora and her family members have also been summoned in a probe pertaining to money laundering. Devinderjit Singh Dhos, MLA from the Dharamkot assembly constituency, has been asked to appear at its Chandigarh zonal office on November 27.

Article Title: Motha MLA flags seat-sharing imbalance ahead of civic polls
Article Text:
Agartala:





Ahead of the Nov 27 urban local body elections in Tripura, TIPRA Motha MLA Ranjit Debbarma has voiced dissatisfaction over the NDA ’s proposed seat-sharing arrangement, saying his party has been allotted fewer seats than expected in the Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC).Debbarma said TIPRA Motha had hoped to contest a larger number of AMC seats and had held several rounds of discussions with alliance partners to seek a more favourable deal.The party had initially sought an equitable share of the nine reserved seats but was eventually offered only three. Talks of friendly contests on the remaining seats also failed to materialise, he said.On the independent candidature of Purabi Debbarma from AMC Ward 19, Ranjit said she had considerable support within TIPRA Motha, including from leaders, workers and supporters.“Purabi, a member of the Motha’s women wing’s central committee, has built strong organizational ties that enhance her candidacy. She receives support from both tribal and Bengali communities in Krishnanagar area of the city,” he said.Ranjit, however, said he would not campaign for her because she was contesting as an Independent, even as some party members had chosen to support her voluntarily.He also criticised coordination among NDA partners, alleging that BJP ministers had not adequately backed TIPRA Motha candidates in Bishramganj, Sabroom and Ambassa.The party’s upcoming central working committee meeting is expected to focus on resolving the seat-sharing dispute and improving coordination within the alliance, he said.Debbarma also expressed optimism over ongoing discussions in Delhi on tribal rights. A committee examining land-related demands is expected to submit its recommendations in the first week of Dec, he said. Implementing them may require amendments to the Tripura Land Revenue and Land Reforms Act, 1960.Despite the alliance-related concerns, Debbarma expressed confidence in TIPRA Motha’s electoral prospects and urged voters to exercise their democratic rights freely and elect candidates who can address local issues effectively.
Article Summary: TIPRA Motha MLA Ranjit Debbarma has voiced dissatisfaction over the NDA ’s proposed seat-sharing arrangement. He said his party has been allotted fewer seats than expected in the Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC)

Article Title: Yet to decide on delimitation bill: Supriya Sule; support does not mean joining NDA, says Tatkare
Article Text:
Supriya Sule

Thane/Pune:





Days after she said her party was in principle willing to offer conditional support to the Centre’s delimitation bill, NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule on Sunday said they had not received the proposed legislation and would take a clear stand only after examining it.The remarks came on a day Sunil Tatkare, the state unit chief of the rival party, dismissed media reports suggesting that NCP (SP) was moving closer to BJP , calling them unfounded. He said NCP (SP)’s stand on supporting the bill did not mean that it would join NDA . “Its stand seems to have been taken in the larger democratic interest. Supriya Sule’s support is based on a matter of principle—the core of the country’s parliamentary democratic system—and her statement is certainly welcome,” he said in Pune. He rejected claims that five NCP (SP) MPs were preparing to switch sides, calling them “fabricated stories” and baseless allegations that undermined democratic discourse.He said Lok Sabha and assembly seats had remained frozen since 1971, despite India’s population having quadrupled to 140 crore. He said the proposed delimitation legislation was a necessary step towards ensuring fair representation.Asked about Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut’s claims of Rs 150 crore being offered to opposition MPs for supporting the bill, Sule said in Thane everyone had the right to make allegations in a democracy.She expressed serious concern over the rising crime rate in Maharashtra , warning that her party would launch an agitation if the police administration failed to improve the law and order situation.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule said they had not received the proposed legislation and would take a clear stand only after examining it. Sunil Tatkare, the state unit chief of the rival party, dismissed media reports suggesting that NCP ( SP) was moving closer to BJP. He said NCP’s stand did not mean that it would join NDA.

Article Title: ​Rajya Sabha MP Wadkute passes away
Article Text:
Ramrao Wadkute

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Rajya Sabha member and BJP leader Ramrao Wadkute died at AIIMS in New Delhi late on Saturday after suffering a severe heart attack. He was 72.Wadkute was admitted to AIIMS on Nov 20 after complaining of cough and chest discomfort. He suffered a heart attack and died while undergoing treatment, party leaders said.A resident of Kalamnuri in Hingoli district, Wadkute was a prominent leader of the Dhangar community in Marathwada and was known as a simple, grassroots politician.Condoling his death, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said Wadkute’s demise was the loss of a simple and dedicated political leader who was deeply committed to grassroots welfare.“He shouldered many organizational responsibilities for the BJP in Hingoli district. He did a great deal of work for the Dhangar community. He left his mark on the cooperative sector as well. His concern for grassroots communities was always evident,” the CM said.Wadkute began his political career with Nationalist Congress Party and served as a member of Maharashtra Legislative Council from June 2014 to Oct 2019. He was also president of Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Maharashtra Sheep and Goat Development Corporation Limited.He left the NCP in Oct 2019 and joined the BJP. In 2021, he was appointed BJP’s Hingoli district president. He also served as the party’s election chief and in-charge for the Hingoli Lok Sabha constituency. The BJP nominated him for the Rajya Sabha from Maharashtra in March this year.BJP Hingoli district president Gajanan Ghuge said last rites on Wadkute were scheduled on Tuesday morning. “His body will be flown to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Monday, and will be taken to Parbhani first and later at Hingoli. The last rites will be performed when his daughter arrives from the US,” he said.Wadkute is survived by his wife, two sons and a daughter.
Article Summary: Wadkute was admitted to AIIMS on Nov 20 after complaining of cough and chest discomfort. He suffered a heart attack and died while undergoing treatment, party leaders said. He was a prominent leader of the Dhangar community in Marathwada.

Article Title: Raut claims Rs 150cr being offered to MPs to back delimitation bill, Mahajan says allegations childish
Article Text:
File photo

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut claimed on Saturday that MPs were being offered “Rs 150 crore to back the proposed delimitation bill”, even as BJP minister Girish Mahajan dismissed it as a “childish allegation”.Raut also said that BJP would not return to power in 2029 if the current political atmosphere and public pressure continued. He added that Congress party’s performance in Rajasthan’s panchayat elections reflected the country’s changing mood.Interacting with the media during his visit to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Saturday, Raut alleged that BJP was attempting to secure support for the proposed delimitation bill and questioned why a Parliament session was not being convened.“Remember this figure if Maharashtra ’s MPs support the bill,” Raut said, alleging that some prominent politicians in the state had been entrusted with arranging the money and securing support. He also questioned Union home minister Amit Shah ’s frequent visits to Mumbai over the past two months, alleging that political negotiations were being conducted from the city.BJP minister Girish Mahajan, speaking in Jalgaon, said that Raut makes “childish allegations.No one takes him seriously anymore.”Raut said Congress’s good performance in Rajasthan’s panchayat samiti and zilla parishad elections was the outcome of public pressure preventing electoral malpractice and keeping the election machinery under check. “If this public pressure continues until 2029, the BJP will not return to power. It is not 100% but 500% certain,” he said.

Article Title: Five in custody for smuggling pangolin body parts in Karvir
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





Forest department officials arrested five men for allegedly trying to sell 5 kg of pangolin scales and other body parts at Mauje Karanjfen village in Karvir taluka.Acting on a tip-off, teams from the Karvir and Panhala forest ranges laid a trap and caught the accused. Officials seized the pangolin parts from them.The accused were identified as Lahu Dhaku Hadkar (60) of Kankavali taluka in Sindhudurg district and Dnyandev Sattu Savare (46), Prakash Shankar Patil (50), Nathaji Yashwant Patil (39) and Bajirao Bandopant Malave (38), all from Shahuwadi taluka in Kolhapur district.A case was registered under the Wildlife (Protection) Act and the accused were produced before a court.Pangolins receive the highest level of legal protection under Schedule I of the Act. Article Summary: Forest department officials arrested five men for allegedly trying to sell 5 kg of pangolin scales and other body parts. Teams from Karvir and Panhala forest ranges laid a trap and caught the accused. Pangolins receive the highest level of legal protection under Schedule I of the Act.

Article Title: Constable heads probe against sr PI, HC orders fresh inquiry at DCP-level
Article Text:
Nagpur:





The Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court recently directed that a DCP-level officer conduct an investigation into a complaint against the senior police inspector of a police station in the city, after it was found that the earlier probe had been carried out by a head constable under the same inspector.A division bench comprising Justices Urmila Joshi-Phalke and Raj D Wakode on Thursday said the earlier probe went “against the principles of natural justice”, while directing the fresh investigation be completed within three months.The case involves an inquiry following a complaint filed by the petitioner against the inspector alleging pressure exerted for repayment of a loan. The petitioner claimed that he took a hand loan of Rs10 lakh from an acquaintance and repaid it despite facing difficulties during Covid-19.The petitioner’s counsel, RP Joshi, submitted that his client was called to a police station in Sept 2023 for recovery of the amount. The petitioner claims he was humiliated on a subsequent visit and was forced to give an undertaking for repayment.In Jan 2024, he filed a complaint with the commissioner of police (CP) against the senior PI of the police station. The petitioner claimed that in April, the complaint was forwarded to DCP, Zone 1, who passed it on to the same police station, where a head constable held the inquiry.The petitioner also alleged that the inquiry was conducted in his absence. Additional public prosecutor (APP) SS Hulke informed the court that a WhatsApp notice was sent, but the petitioner did not appear. The APP added that they have no objection to an inquiry by a superior officer.VS Mishra, counsel for both the lender and Sr PI, submitted that no explanation was given as to why the complaint was filed with the CP after four months of the said incident. The counsel added that questions raised by the petitioner are of “disputed facts”, for which evidence is required, and therefore the writ petition is not maintainable.The bench found that “no proper notice was served upon the petitioner by the inquiry officer” and that the petitioner was given no chance to put forward his grievances. The whole grievance, the bench noted, was against the senior PI, while the inquiry was held by a head constable working under that inspector.Ordering an inquiry by a DCP-level officer, the court said the petitioner should be given due opportunity to appear and present evidence or arguments.
Article Summary: Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court recently directed that a DCP-level officer conduct an investigation into a complaint against the senior police inspector. The case involves an inquiry following a complaint filed by the petitioner against the inspector alleging pressure exerted for repayment of a loan. The petitioner claimed that he took a hand loan of Rs10 lakh from an acquaintance and repaid it despite facing difficulties during Covid-19.

Article Title: Four held arrested in Ghoti robbery case
Article Text:
Nashik:





The Nashik Rural police have arrested four suspects allegedly involved in a night-time robbery on Khodala Road in the Devgaon area, under the Ghoti police station limits.The accused have been identified as Kashinath Khode (29) and Sanjay Bhangre (30), residents of Bhilmal, and Vaibhav Zole (19) and Kiran Khade (29), residents of Dhadoshi. All four are from Trimbakeshwar taluka in Nashik district.The robbery occurred on the night of Nov 16. According to the complaint filed by Sagar Shedwal, a resident of Pen in Raigad district, he was travelling by car with his family when unidentified persons allegedly blocked their vehicle using another car.The accused reportedly threatened Shedwal and his family members at knifepoint before forcibly taking gold ornaments, cash, an ATM card, and a driving licence, together valued at Rs 1.74 lakh. They then fled in their car.On Shedwal’s complaint, the Ghoti police registered a case of armed robbery under relevant sections of the BNS. “Soon after receiving information about the robbery, a patrolling team from Ghoti police station visited the scene,” a police officer said.Guided by senior officers, Local Crime Branch inspector Rahul More and Ghoti police station inspector Vijay Shinde gathered confidential intelligence based on the modus operandi of the criminals, their descriptions, dialect and the vehicle used in the crime.Police arrested four suspects during a search in Trimbakeshwar taluka. During interrogation, they admitted to committing the crime with accomplices. Police also seized the sports utility vehicle used in the crime and their cell phones.
Article Summary: Nashik Rural police have arrested four suspects allegedly involved in a night- time robbery. The accused have been identified as Kashinath Khode, Sanjay Bhangre, Vaibhav Zole and Kiran Khade. All four are from Trimbakeshwar taluka in Nashik district.

Article Title: TNEB employee held with ganja in Mettur
Article Text:
Salem





: A suspended electricity board employee was arrested on Saturday for smuggling ganja on his two-wheeler in Mettur.Police identified the arrested person as M Joseph, 47, of Matha Kovil area in Mettur. According to an investigation officer, Joseph was nabbed while they were conducting a routine vehicle check along the right bank of Mettur dam on Kolathur Road.“He was riding a two-wheeler in a suspicious manner. We seized the contraband and took Joseph to the police station for interrogation.”Investigations revealed that Joseph was already facing a ganja smuggling case, which had led to his suspension from the electricity board.Police registered a case, arrested him and produced him before the Mettur court, which remanded him in judicial custody. Article Title: Traffic diversions announced in Krishnagiri in view of festivals
Article Text:
traffic diversions

Krishnagiri

:





District police have announced traffic diversions for heavy vehicles and non-pilgrim traffic from 2pm on November 22 to 6am on November 26, in view of Tiruvannamalai Maharatham and Karthigai Deepam festivals.In a media statement, SP GS Anitha stated that heavy vehicles travelling from Bengaluru to Tiruvannamalai , Villupuram, Cuddalore and Puducherry must take the Krishnagiri-Vaniyambadi-Vellore-Cheyyar-Vandavasi-Tindivanam route instead of proceeding through Uthangarai, Chengam and Tiruvannamalai.Vehicles from Bengaluru bound for Vriddhachalam, Chidambaram and Nagapattinam through Krishnagiri will be diverted via Dharmapuri, Thoppur, Salem, Vazhapadi, and Attur.Vehicles from Bargur towards Tiruvannamalai and those arriving through Kuppam will be diverted via Vaniyambadi, Vellore, Cheyyar, Vandavasi, and Tindivanam. Heavy vehicles arriving from Dharmapuri through Manjamedu will be diverted at Puliyur Junction towards Tiruvannamalai Road instead of Pochampally Road.Heavy vehicles travelling from Krishnagiri towards Tiruvannamalai will be diverted to Bargur Road at Jagadevi.All vehicles heading from Krishnagiri to Tiruvannamalai will also be diverted at Kannandahalli near Mathur police station towards Tirupattur.Heavy vehicles using Krishnagiri bypass roads will be diverted at Uthangarai MGR Nagar through Karapattu, Kathavani and Arunapathi toll road towards Tirupattur. Those arriving from Salem via Harur and Uthangarai for Tiruvannamalai will also be redirected through Tirupattur.Heavy vehicles travelling from Tirupattur towards Tiruvannamalai via Singarapettai and Chengam will be rerouted towards Tirupattur. Vehicles from Dharmapuri district proceeding via Irumathur, Puliyur, and Olapatti will use alternative routes notified by police.The SP explained the arrangements at a consultation meeting with truck drivers’ welfare association office-bearers at the district police office and sought their cooperation.
Article Summary: Heavy vehicles travelling from Bengaluru to Tiruvannamalai must take the Krishnagiri-Vaniyambadi-Vellore-Cheyyar-Vandavasi-Tindivanam route. Vehicles from Dharmapuri district proceeding via Irumathur, Puliyur, and Olapatti will use alternative routes.

Article Title: Rash and wrong-side driving: Coimbatore district police book driver, seize private bus, recommend cancellation of licence and permit
Article Text:

COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore district police have seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving at Pappampatti Pirivu on the Coimbatore–Palladam Road.According to a statement issued by the district police on Tuesday, the incident occurred around 8.30am on Monday while the private bus was heading to Coimbatore from Tirupur. Article Summary: The Coimbatore district police seized a private mofussil bus and booked its driver for rash, negligent and wrong-side driving. Driver Sakthivel drove the bus at a high speed before abruptly swerving the vehicle to the right and driving against the oncoming traffic.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: HC judge questions police inaction on harassment complaint against TVK MLA
Article Text: Madurai: Madras high court judge Justice L Victoria Gowri has questioned the alleged police inaction over sexual harassment allegations against TVK’s Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh, who is accused of sending obscene messages to district collector J E Padmaja.Speaking at a workplace sexual harassment awareness programme organised by the Madras high court’s Gender Sensitisation and Internal Complaints Committee-II at Lady Doak College on Saturday, she asked, “Isn’t that workplace harassment?” Referring to the alleged messages, she said the collector’s husband had lodged a complaint, but the state police had remained indifferent.The remarks come amid mounting pressure on the TVK govt over the allegations, with DMK MP Kanimozhi and other opposition leaders demanding action against the legislator. Law minister CTR Nirmal Kumar, however, dismissed the allegations as baseless and accused Kanimozhi of amplifying unverified social media claims. Vignesh also denied any wrongdoing, describing the controversy as politically motivated.Revenue minister K A Sengottaiyan subsequently acknowledged receiving an explanation from the MLA, which was forwarded to the collector. The National Commission for Women has also sought an impartial police inquiry into the allegations.Earlier, Justice Gowri recalled poet Subramania Bharathi’s advocacy of gender equality and cited the Bhanwari Devi gang-rape case in Rajasthan and the Rupan Deol Bajaj-KPS Gill case to illustrate workplace harassment. She stressed that women remained vulnerable to harassment irrespective of their professional positions and urged men to respect the dignity, personal boundaries and professional space of their female colleagues.
Article Summary: Madras high court judge Justice L Victoria Gowri questioned the alleged police inaction over sexual harassment allegations. TVK’s Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh is accused of sending obscene messages to district collector J E Padmaja.

Article Title: Cop suspended over drunken brawl
Article Text: Dindigul: A head constable was suspended from service for assaulting a man during a drunken altercation in Nilakottai on Nov 19.Police said Palpandithurai, a head constable with Ammayanayakanur highway patrol division, and one Arivazhagan had been involved in a dispute for the past two years. On Nov 19, the policeman and his friend, Arul, were consuming alcohol near Duraisamypuram when Arivazhagan arrived at the same place with an alcohol bottle.An argument allegedly broke out and Palpandithurai and Arul assaulted Arivazhagan with their hands and pushed him to the ground. Arivazhagan sustained a head injury and was admitted to Dindigul Govt Medical College Hospital, where he is undergoing treatment.Nilakottai police registered a case against Palpandithurai and Arul. Superintendent of police S Jeyakumar ordered that the head constable be placed under suspension, and directed a departmental inquiry into his conduct.
Article Summary: A head constable was suspended from service for assaulting a man during a drunken altercation in Nilakottai on Nov 19. Police said Palpandithurai and one Arivazhagan had been involved in a dispute for the past two years. The policeman and his friend, Arul, were consuming alcohol near Duraisamypuram.

Article Title: Govt school teacher arrested under POCSO Act in Salem district

SALEM: A govt school teacher was arrested in Salem district on Sunday night under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act on charges of inappropriate behaviour towards girl students.The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district.According to the complaint, the teacher allegedly made inappropriate remarks to Class X girl students on Nov 5. “He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’ while commenting on the beauty of her eyes,” said an officer at the all women police station in Attur.The students brought the matter to the notice of the headmaster on Nov 13. The headmaster informed chief educational officer A Ellappan and contacted Childline 1098 seeking intervention.Following the complaint, a member of the child welfare committee visited the school on Nov 14 and conducted an inquiry into the allegations raised by the students.Based on the findings, the headmaster lodged a complaint with the Attur all women police on Sunday. Police registered a case against Sankar and arrested him. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested teacher, M Sankar, 49, of Vinayagapuram, is serving as a social science teacher in a govt school in the district. He is accused of making a heart-shaped hand gesture towards one student and calling another student ‘Cleopatra’

Article Title: Man suspected to have died by suicide after jumping in front of train in Varkala
Article Text:
Thiruvananthapuram

:





A 56-year-old man is suspected to have died by suicide after allegedly jumping in front of a moving train near Maithanam Junction in Varkala early on Sunday.The deceased was Kumar T, 56, of Kuruvila in Varkala. The incident occurred around 5.30am near the old railway gate.According to the police, preliminary information suggests that Kumar jumped in front of a train. The locals who spotted the body informed the police.Varkala Police shifted the body to Varkala govt taluk hospital. The body will be handed over to the relatives after postmortem. The police said the deceased was unmarried.Varkala police have registered a case of unnatural death and initiated further proceedings to ascertain the circumstances leading to the incident.

Article Title: Two youths booked for knocking down excise officer with motorcycle in Thodupuzha
Article Text:
Thodupuzha

:





The police have registered a case against two youths who allegedly knocked down and grievously injured an excise inspector with their motorcycle during vehicle checks at Mattupara in Kumaramangalam on Saturday.The accused are Tenz, 23, of Kadavoor, Kothamangalam, who was riding the motorcycle, and Rohith, 22, of Mutharamkunnu, Kumaramangalam, who was riding pillion.The police said a team led by Thodupuzha range excise inspector Lijo Oommen was inspecting vehicles when officers signalled the motorcycle to stop. The rider allegedly accelerated and rammed the inspector. The motorcycle ran over his leg before overturning, injuring both riders.Oommen suffered grievous injuries to his right knee and wounds on his hands and legs. He was admitted to a private hospital in Thodupuzha.During the inspection, officers allegedly recovered four grams of ganja from Tenz and three grams from Rohith. Based on Oommen’s statement recorded at the hospital, the police registered the case under relevant sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Article Summary: The police have registered a case against two youths who allegedly knocked down and grievously injured an excise inspector with their motorcycle. The accused are Tenz, 23, of Kadavoor, Kothamangalam, who was riding the motorcycle, and Rohith, 22, of Mutharamkunnu.

Article Title: Woman found hanging in Garhwa; kin allege murder
Article Text:
Photo for representation only

Garhwa

:





The body of a 40-year-old woman was found hanging in her house in Tamge Kalan village under Ranka police station limits of the district on Monday. The deceased was identified as Kunjan Devi. While Kunjan’s in-laws claimed she had died by suicide, her mother alleged she was murdered by her husband and father-in-law for her property.Kunjan’s family claimed she had inherited her father’s property along with her two sisters after their father’s death. Kunjan’s husband Vikas Paswan was allegedly eyeing her father’s property and used to beat her. The couple had an argument two days ago.Vishnu Kant, the officer-in-charge of Ranka police station, said, “The body of the deceased was sent to Garhwa Sadar Hospital for post-mortem examination. It can only be ascertained after the receiving post-mortem report that whether the matter is related to murder or suicide.”
Article Summary: The body of a 40-year-old woman was found hanging in her house in Tamge Kalan village under Ranka police station limits of the district on Monday. The deceased was identified as Kunjan Devi. Her in-laws claimed she had died by suicide, her mother alleged she was murdered by her husband and father-in-law for her property.
